clue.text: Affected by skinhead, a rogue

blocks.note: read as skin's head: the first letter of skin
camp means affected, theatrically exaggerated

explanation.surface: Someone is influenced by a shaven-headed thug who is a bit of a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' looks like one word for a thug, but it splits into skin's head; that letter goes in front of the word for affected.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous rascal, a mild word for a rogue or scoundrel.

clue.text: Right in the main

blocks.note: surface reading: correct for the most part, by and large
setter's reading: the main is the open sea, so this is the right-hand side at sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' is the idiom for mostly; the main is also the old word for the sea, where right is named differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Starboard is the nautical term for the right-hand side of a vessel when facing forward.

clue.text: The place, of course, to produce Tosca

indicators.note: the answer's letters must be worked over to produce the opera, so this is rearrangement run in reverse

blocks.note: Puccini's opera, taken as written

explanation.surface: A venue that is naturally the right place to stage Puccini's opera.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: rearrange the answer and you produce Tosca. Ascot is an English racecourse, home of Royal Ascot, so it is the place of course.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a famous racecourse in Berkshire, so it is a place with a course for horse racing.

clue.text: Advertise for a title?

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
a claim is a title or right to something, as in a legal claim

explanation.surface: Seeking a title by putting a notice in the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that 'for a title' is not a reason for advertising but two pieces of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim is to announce publicly, to make something widely known, as advertising does.

clue.text: No longer forced to serve, so moved

blocks.note: first meaning, an old one: pressed into service in the navy or army, as by a press gang
second meaning: emotionally struck or affected

explanation.surface: A conscript, freed from compulsory service, is touched by the release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' does not mean freed: it marks the first sense as archaic, the way press gangs once forced men into the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Impressed once meant compelled into military service; today it means touched or affected emotionally, as moved does.

clue.text: Some could hide a secret, it's thought

indicators.note: some of the words means only a part of them is used, a run of consecutive letters

blocks.note: the letters run across hide and a

explanation.surface: Some people are believed to be able to keep a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or notion, something produced in the mind by thinking.

clue.text: After many an adjustment of rates this is official

indicators.note: an adjustment alters the arrangement of something, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: post is Latin for after, as in postwar
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a large number
the letters of rates, rearranged

explanation.surface: After yet another change to the postal rates, this is how it officially stands.
explanation.walkthrough: The rates surface suggests postal charges, apt for an official of the post office.
explanation.definitionFit: A postmaster is the official in charge of a post office, a public functionary.

clue.text: Put money into comforts - they're so supportive

indicators.note: to put something into another thing is to place it inside, so one part goes within the other

blocks.note: eases means comforts, soothes
L is the abbreviation for pound, the old pound sterling sign

explanation.surface: Investing in comfortable things because they are such a support.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for the pound, Britain's currency, from Latin libra; it goes inside EASES.
explanation.definitionFit: Easels are stands that hold up a painter's canvas, so they literally give it support.

clue.text: Declaration by country people on their leader

indicators.note: the leader is the one in front, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: a state is a country or nation
men are people
the first letter of their

explanation.surface: A nation's people issue a pronouncement about the person in charge of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their leader' suggests a head of state; it is only the first letter of the word their.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement is a formal announcement or assertion, which is what a declaration is.

clue.text: Note the evidence of a hard blow remained

blocks.note: D is a note of the musical scale

blocks.clueFragment: the evidence of a hard blow
blocks.note: a welt is a raised mark left on the skin by a blow

explanation.surface: Pay attention: the bruise from the hard punch stayed for days.
explanation.walkthrough: Note looks like the verb take notice; it is a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to stay or live somewhere, so dwelt means stayed on, lived, or remained.

clue.text: Social workers with inside job — they don't go out

indicators.note: having something inside means one word sits within the other

blocks.note: ants are social insects and are workers
a chore is a job or task

explanation.surface: Social workers who have an in-house post never leave the office.
explanation.walkthrough: Social workers are not council staff here but insects that live in colonies; the job goes inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchorets, or anchorites, are religious recluses who shut themselves away and never leave their cells.

clue.text: Over-slender

blocks.note: first meaning: left over, extra
second meaning: lean, thin

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen makes one word, too thin, but the clue is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare describes something surplus or left over, and also a lean, thin figure.

clue.text: A flask for spirit

blocks.note: first meaning: a container for liquid
second meaning: courage, nerve, in British slang

explanation.surface: A hip flask meant for carrying whisky or gin.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirit looks like the drink the flask holds; it is the British slang sense of nerve or courage, as in 'lose your bottle'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle is a narrow-necked vessel like a flask, and in British slang bottle means courage or nerve.

clue.text: Hits back in case it's of the least significance

indicators.note: going back means the word is written from its end to its start

blocks.note: to lam is to thrash or beat
lest means in case, for fear that

explanation.surface: Someone strikes back just in case a small matter turns out to matter.
explanation.walkthrough: LAMS read backwards gives SMAL, then LEST completes SMALLEST. Lam is an old word for beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Smallest is the superlative of small, the thing that matters least or is of minimum importance.

clue.text: In the middle of Victoria team cannot have a drink

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its centre, so only its central letters are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the two central letters of Victoria
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a cricket or football team
can't is the short form of cannot

explanation.surface: Players stuck at Victoria station are not allowed even one drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun: the answer names something that intoxicates, an alcoholic drink. Victoria is a London railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: An intoxicant is anything that makes you drunk, such as alcohol in a strong drink.

clue.text: Taking in a dress to reshape, showing expertise

indicators.note: to reshape something is to give it a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dressmaker skilfully takes in a frock, altering it to fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking in' sounds like dressmaking; here it means the word in is taken along with a dress to, and all ten letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroitness is skill or dexterity, the cleverness with hands or mind that expertise implies.

clue.text: Shedding tears isn't hard!

indicators.note: shedding scatters things loosely, so these letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone claims that crying is easy, which is not difficult at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Hard is not the opposite of easy here but means tough, unyielding.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resistant withstands force or pressure, which is what a hard, tough material does.

clue.text: Edge along the pedestrian way

blocks.note: surface reading: to sidle or creep slowly along a footpath
setter's reading: the edge running along a pavement, the walkers' way

explanation.walkthrough: 'Edge along' reads as a verb for moving sideways; it is the noun, the border of the pavement. Kerb is the British spelling of curb.
explanation.definitionFit: The kerb is the raised stone border between a pavement and the road, its outer limit.

clue.text: Counsel winning or one prepared to compromise?

blocks.note: the bar is the body of barristers who serve as counsel
a gainer is one who wins or profits

explanation.surface: A lawyer either wins the case or is willing to settle.
explanation.walkthrough: The bar is the legal profession; read the answer as bar gainer, the bar winning, and the question mark admits the stretch. 'or' offers it as an alternative reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargainer is someone who haggles and negotiates, ready to meet the other side partway in a deal.

clue.text: Club assessment is steep

blocks.note: a mace is a heavy club used as a weapon
a rate is a valuation, and rates were a British local property tax

explanation.surface: The golf club's annual fee is very expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: Steep looks like an adjective for a high price; it is the verb to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To macerate is to soften food by soaking it in liquid, which is what steeping means.

clue.text: A suggestion to discourage

blocks.note: first meaning: a small amount, a hint or touch
second meaning: to dishearten, as in hopes being crushed

explanation.surface: Offering a hint intended to put someone off.
explanation.definitionFit: A dash of something is a tiny trace or hint, and to dash hopes is to crush or deflate someone's spirits.

clue.text: Far-sighted person in favour of keeping serving men standing

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it, so one part is held within another

blocks.note: for means in support of
RE is the Royal Engineers, soldiers in service
caste is social rank or standing

explanation.surface: A visionary backs keeping soldiers on their feet, ready to serve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in favour of' is split open to hold the rest. The Royal Engineers are a corps of the British Army, so serving men in crossword shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecaster predicts what lies ahead, so is literally someone who sees far into the future.

clue.text: Read about mould, required for a tropical pot-plant

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: to con is to study or read carefully
rot is decay, like mould

explanation.surface: Studying mould, as needed to keep an exotic house plant healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read is the old sense of con, to study or pore over; the decay word goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Croton is a tropical shrub with bright variegated leaves, widely grown indoors as a house plant.

clue.text: Others fall out of control

blocks.note: the rest are the others
rain is a fall of water from the sky

explanation.surface: Other people tumble about, having lost all control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall out of control' reads as a phrase about chaos; the definition is control alone, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain someone is to hold them back or keep them in check, which is to control them.

clue.text: Quickly took steps against the opposition

blocks.note: first meaning: ran fast, hurried
second meaning: competed with rivals in a contest of speed

explanation.surface: Someone acted promptly to deal with their opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took steps against' reads as taking action against rivals; the steps are real strides, and the second half is the contest sense of the same verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To have run at speed, and to have competed in a contest of speed, are both senses of the past tense of race.

clue.text: A green alternative of sorts

indicators.note: an alternative is another version, so these letters come in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sort of eco-friendly option, a Green political choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green alternative' sounds like an environmental choice, but alternative signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Genera, plural of genus, are classes or kinds, a biological word for sorts of living things.

clue.text: Oriental ruler stretching

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for east, the Orient
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: An Eastern monarch reaching out or extending his empire.
explanation.walkthrough: Stretching is in the sense of eking out, making a supply last longer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eking out supplies means making them go further, stretching them to last.

clue.text: Quite unfriendly — a common complaint

blocks.note: first meaning: frosty, distant in manner
second meaning: the everyday illness with sniffles

explanation.surface: Someone thoroughly hostile, a frequent grumble about them.
explanation.walkthrough: Complaint looks like a grumble; it is an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold describes a chilly, unwelcoming manner, and a cold is the commonest minor viral illness.

clue.text: Shipping trade

blocks.note: first meaning: boats and vessels collectively
second meaning: a skilled occupation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shipping trade' reads as the business of freight; split it into two meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft is used for vessels collectively, and also for a skilled occupation or handiwork.

clue.text: It turns on a woman's first love

indicators.note: something that turns faces the other way, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: taken as written
Dora is a woman's name
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something that excites a woman's first romantic passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a woman's first' is an order instruction: the woman comes before the turned word and its partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep, worshipful affection, a strong form of love.

clue.text: Blew up when given date to end conversion

indicators.note: a conversion changes one thing into another form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lost their temper when told the deadline for finishing a building conversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blew up' suggests losing one's temper; here it is the literal explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: Detonated means exploded, as a bomb does, which is to blow up in the literal sense.

clue.text: Keen to take silver in always

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so one part goes inside the other

blocks.note: e'er is the poetic short form of ever
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone forever keen to win the silver medal.
explanation.walkthrough: Always is the poetic contraction of ever found in hymns and verse; the metal's chemical symbol sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager means keen, full of enthusiasm and impatient desire for something.
